title: Dispatch: encode the concrete selected interpretation and generalize the jhpt route invariant (attempt 1)
description:
Dispatch child of eshyra-o9bd.19.9 (Transition W7). Read `bd show eshyra-o9bd.19.9`
for the parent spec, and `bd show eshyra-o9bd.19.9.2` for the previous repair
round. This bead repairs the ONE remaining BLOCKING review finding on PR #515,
reviewed at head `c1ac5abe6e37012cdb26997d92b8d12a03e24a40`, profile
`rules-clause-complete`. Read the finding first with
`gh pr view 515 --json comments` (it is the most recent CHANGES REQUIRED
comment).

The previous currency-gate finding is CLOSED and the P7 execution split is
accepted as correctly generalized. Do not redo either. Exact-head CI run
33577075936 is fully green; do not chase CI.

Authority: ADR 0020, design sections 6.2, 8, 10.7, 10.10, and 11 of
docs/audits/rules-awareness-transition/2026-07-30-integrated-transition-design.md.

BRANCH / WORKTREE
Branch `eshyra-o9bd.19.9.3`, worktree `.worktrees/eshyra-o9bd.19.9.3`, cut from
the parent branch `eshyra-o9bd.19.9` at its current head. Work only inside that
worktree; `cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"` after entering it.

The supervisor independently confirmed both halves of this finding against the
code before filing this bead. They are real; implement the repair rather than
re-arguing it, but verify each mechanism yourself as you fix it.

=== HALF A — a resolved ruling must name its selected interpretation ===

Confirmed defect. P7's `with-active-ruling` execution marks the ambiguity
`resolved` and lists BOTH published interpretation ids in `interpretationIds`
(correct — both must stay visible), but neither `campaignRuleState` nor
`expectedCampaignRuleOrRulingState.cases[0]` says WHICH interpretation the
ruling selected. `campaignRuleState` carries only
`{source, ruling: 'active ruling supplied by eshyra-jhpt', scope}`, and the
ruling case carries identity, scope, and provenance but no selection. The oracle
signal claims it supplies the "resolution" while the resolution value is absent.

Consequence: `expectedResolution: 'resolved'` is non-falsifiable for W8. A packet
carrying any ruling — or merely evidence that some ruling exists — would satisfy
the fixture without proving which published interpretation governs the campaign.
The accepted design defines the `campaign-ruling` route evidence as ruling
identity, ambiguity id, AND selected interpretation id, and records that
`eshyra-jhpt.1` already requires a ruling to carry the ambiguity id and selected
interpretation id as provenance. This matters even though `use_item` stays
readiness-blocked: discovery must still place the concrete campaign ruling beside
the ambiguity before DM adjudication.

REQUIRED REPAIR

1. Add `selectedInterpretationId` to `AmbiguityExpectation`.
   - REQUIRED when `expectedResolution === 'resolved'`.
   - FORBIDDEN when `expectedResolution === 'unresolved'` — an unresolved
     ambiguity cannot name a selection, and making the field's meaning
     conditional-but-unambiguous is the point.
   - The validator must reject a `selectedInterpretationId` that is not a member
     of that same expectation's declared `interpretationIds`.

2. Complete the route-evidence triple on the ruling record itself, so a consumer
   can recover identity + ambiguity id + selected interpretation id from the
   ruling case without cross-referencing by convention. A `CampaignRuleCase`
   with `ruleKind: 'ruling'` that resolves an ambiguity must carry the ambiguity
   id and the selected interpretation id, and the validator must reject
   disagreement between the ruling case and the corresponding
   `AmbiguityExpectation`. Model the new ruling-case fields explicitly rather
   than overloading the free-text `scope` string.

3. The currency test must validate `selectedInterpretationId` against the PACK:
   it must resolve as an actual published interpretation id on the named
   ambiguity of the named record (reuse the existing interpretation lookup that
   already checks `interpretationIds`). An unknown or stale selection must fail.

4. P7's `with-active-ruling` execution selects ONE concrete interpretation.
   Recommended: `same-face-resets`, which matches the fixture's player input
   (pressing the already-active face) — but whichever you choose, it is an
   ORACLE-SUPPLIED value owned by eshyra-jhpt, NOT a fact derived from the pack.
   The pack's `canonicalResolution` is null and must stay that way. State that
   distinction in-band, and update the `jhpt-active-ruling` oracle signal's
   `supplies` text so it names the concrete selected interpretation rather than
   a generic "resolution".

5. `without-active-ruling` is unchanged: still `unresolved`, still no
   `campaign-ruling` route, still no selected interpretation, and both published
   interpretations still visible.

6. Capability status stays `blocked` in BOTH executions. The ruling resolves
   interpretation only; it does not make an engine-pending readiness clause
   green. Do not let this change weaken that.

Negative regression evidence required (add to the adversarial mutation test):
  - a resolved expectation with `selectedInterpretationId` removed → rejected;
  - a `selectedInterpretationId` that is not in the declared
    `interpretationIds` → rejected by the validator;
  - a `selectedInterpretationId` that is well-formed but does not exist as a
    published interpretation on the pack's ambiguity (stale/unknown) → rejected
    by the currency assertions;
  - a ruling case whose selected interpretation disagrees with the
    `AmbiguityExpectation` → rejected;
  - an `unresolved` expectation carrying a `selectedInterpretationId` →
    rejected.

=== HALF B — generalize the jhpt state<->route invariant to campaign-rule ===

Confirmed defect. `fixtureContract.ts` around the `noActiveRuling` block
implements only the RULING half: it forbids a `campaign-ruling` route when
`campaignRuleState.kind === 'none'`, and requires one when a case has
`ruleKind: 'ruling'`. There is no symmetric rule for `ruleKind: 'house-rule'`
and the `campaign-rule` route. So the validator would today accept either of:
  - P10 changed to `campaignRuleState: none(...)` while keeping its
    `campaign-rule` route;
  - P10's active house-rule expectation with the `campaign-rule` route removed.
P10 is presently correct, which is exactly why it needs the guard.

REQUIRED REPAIR

Generalize the rule rather than pasting a second hardcoded copy. Drive it from a
single mapping of rule kind to its route class —
`ruling` → `campaign-ruling`, `house-rule` → `campaign-rule` — and apply both
directions uniformly:
  - `campaignRuleState.kind === 'none'` forbids EITHER route;
  - an active `campaignRuleState` with a case of a given `ruleKind` REQUIRES
    that kind's route class.
Keep the error messages specific enough to name which kind and which route.

Negative regression evidence required:
  - P10 mutated to `campaignRuleState: none(...)` while retaining the
    `campaign-rule` route → rejected;
  - P10's `campaign-rule` route removed while the active house-rule case remains
    → rejected;
  - both existing ruling-side mutations still rejected (do not regress them).

HARD CONSTRAINTS
- Test-only. No production code, generated pack data, or schema changes.
- P7 and P10 remain CONSUMERS of the eshyra-jhpt oracle. Do not create a
  discovery-owned ruling store, schema, resolver, or lifecycle (design §8.4).
  The selected interpretation id is oracle-supplied data recorded in the
  fixture, not a resolution this corpus computes.
- Do not change any other fixture's meaning. If a hardened check makes a real
  fixture fail, the fixture's claim was wrong — fix the claim and say so
  in-band, never weaken the check.
- No fixture asserts a count of records; no coverage, readiness, or
  completeness figure over the corpus.
- Every fixture keeps its bounded-evidence statement and `verifiedAtCommit`.
- Do not weaken or edit any existing test or audit expectation.
- Keep the DiagnosticFixture type and FIXTURE_KEYS/EXECUTION_KEYS in sync. A
  previous round shipped a type that declared a field the validator rejected,
  invisible because `test/**` is outside `tsc --build`. If you add a field to a
  type, add it to the matching key set and its validation in the same change.

VERIFICATION
`npm run verify:worktree` from the worktree root, BEFORE committing (it rewrites
files). Expected: all non-skipped tests pass; documented skips are the live-API
integration tests and the Dolt-gated checkpoint tests. The one acceptable Biome
finding is the pre-existing biome.json schema-version info (config 2.5.5,
installed 2.5.10).

Before you finish, prove your new negative evidence is NOT vacuous: temporarily
disable each new validator rule, confirm the corresponding mutation test fails,
then restore. Report that you did it and what you observed.
acceptance_criteria: AmbiguityExpectation carries selectedInterpretationId, required when resolved and forbidden when unresolved, validated as a member of the declared interpretationIds and as a published interpretation on the pack's ambiguity. A ruling CampaignRuleCase carries the ambiguity id and selected interpretation id in explicit fields, and disagreement with the AmbiguityExpectation is rejected. P7's with-active-ruling execution names one concrete oracle-supplied interpretation, labelled as jhpt-owned and not pack-derived, with canonicalResolution still null; capability status stays blocked in both executions. The state-route invariant is driven by a single ruleKind-to-route mapping covering both ruling/campaign-ruling and house-rule/campaign-rule, enforced in both directions. Adversarial tests reject: missing selection when resolved, selection outside interpretationIds, stale selection absent from the pack, ruling-case/expectation disagreement, selection on an unresolved expectation, P10 inactive-state-with-route, and P10 active-state-without-route. Non-vacuity of each new rule demonstrated and reported. No production code, generated pack data, or schema changes. npm run verify:worktree passes.
